lit.'<p>Además de la lava, una erupción prod:
'

Besides lava, an eruption produces ash fall (harmful to lungs, crops, engines and roofs), pyroclastic flows (very fast, scorching clouds), toxic gases and lahars: mudflows that form when the heat melts the summit glacier, as happens at Villarrica. Lahars follow river channels and can travel far.

'
lit.'<p>Con <b>mucha sílice</b> (andesítico:
'

With a lot of silica (andesitic or rhyolitic) the magma is very viscous and traps the gases. As it rises, pressure drops and the gases expand suddenly, like opening a shaken fizzy drink: the eruption is explosive and throws up an ash column several kilometres high, pyroclasts and pyroclastic flows. The Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) runs from 0 to 8.

'
lit.'<p>Los volcanes también aportan: las ce:
'

Volcanoes also bring benefits: weathered ash forms fertile soils; the internal heat provides geothermal energy (in Chile, the Cerro Pabellón plant in Antofagasta) and hot springs; and their landscapes attract tourism. Volcanic gases also formed the Earth’s early atmosphere and oceans.

'
lit.'<p>Por la subducción de la placa de Naz:
'

Because of the subduction of the Nazca plate, Chile has about 90 geologically active volcanoes. SERNAGEOMIN (the national geology and mining service) monitors them and issues a technical alert (green, yellow, orange or red) according to their activity: earthquakes, ground deformation, gases. Recent examples: Chaitén (2008), Calbuco (2015) and Villarrica (2015). Knowing the evacuation routes is part of prevention.

'
lit.'<p>Si el magma tiene <b>poca sílice</b>:
'

If the magma has little silica (basaltic) it is runny (low viscosity) and gases escape easily. The eruption is effusive: lava pours out in flows that run down the slopes, as in Hawaii. They are spectacular but generally less dangerous to people, because they advance slowly.

'
lit.'<p>Un <b>volcán</b> es una abertura por:
'

A volcano is an opening through which magma (molten rock with dissolved gases) escapes from the interior. Magma gathers in a magma chamber a few kilometres down, rises through the vent and comes out of the crater. As lava and ash pile up eruption after eruption, the cone is built. Outside the volcano, magma is called lava.

'
